slides.3.title: Geography, Climate and Soils of the Dão
slides.3.html:
The Dão DOC lies in the highlands of central Portugal, surrounded on three sides by the Serra da Estrela, Serra do Caramulo and Serra da Açor.

🌡️ A sheltered microclimate

  • The mountains block humid Atlantic air and hot dry air from Spain
  • Summers are warmer than on the coast but cooler than in the Douro, with a mean annual temperature of 12–14°C
  • Annual rainfall of 800–1,000mm is relatively generous, aiding slow ripening
  • A "mild continental climate": dry but not scorching summers, cool winters

🪨 Granite soils

  • Mainly granite and sandy soils with excellent drainage
  • Poor soils keep yields low and give minerality and a delicate palate
  • Acidic soils (pH 4.5–5.5) help preserve the grapes' natural acidity

📊 Key figures

  • DOC area: about 9,800 hectares of vines (planted)
  • Altitude: 400–800m, with some top vineyards above 700m
  • The Dão was historically monopolised by private wineries (1950–1990s), and independent estates rose after 1990
slides.4.title: Core Grapes of the Dão: Touriga Nacional and Encruzado
slides.4.html:
🔴 Red grapes: Touriga Nacional is king

  • Touriga Nacional: the Dão is its place of origin. Here it shows its most elegant and delicate side (lighter than the Douro version, with more prominent violet aromas)
  • Tinta Roriz (Tempranillo): often blended with Touriga Nacional to add fruit
  • Alfrocheiro: a red grape characteristic of the Dão, with blackberry and spice notes and balanced structure
  • Jaen (= Mencía): the Portuguese name for Spain's Mencía, light-bodied with fresh fruit

⚪ White grapes: the shining star Encruzado

  • Encruzado: the Dão's flagship white grape, hailed as "Portugal's Chardonnay"
  • Granite soils give a crisp mineral character, with elegant peach and orange blossom aromas
  • After oak ageing: cream, flint and honey, with markedly greater complexity
  • Strong ageing potential: top wines can reach 10–15 years

🏆 Representative producers

  • Quinta dos Roques: the Encruzado benchmark, also makes top Touriga Nacional reds
  • Quinta da Pellada: natural farming, elegant style
  • Alvaro Castro (Quinta da Pellada): a key figure in the Dão revival

slides.7.title: Dão vs. Douro: Two Great Portuguese Reds Compared
slides.7.items.0.label: Dão (the elegant style)
slides.7.items.0.desc: Granite, 400–800m, cool and slow ripening. Touriga Nacional shows delicate violet aromas, with medium body and a silky finish
slides.7.items.1.label: Douro (the powerful style)
slides.7.items.1.desc: Schist, extreme continental climate, hot ripening. Touriga Nacional shows deep purple fruit, with full body, firmer tannins and 20+ years of ageing potential
slides.7.items.2.label: Dão white (Encruzado)
slides.7.items.2.desc: Mineral and crisp → creamy and complex after oak, comparable with Burgundy. One of Portugal's most age-worthy dry whites
slides.7.items.3.label: Douro white
slides.7.items.3.desc: Mainly Rabigato・Gouveio and similar grapes, mineral and crisp, but lighter in structure than Encruzado with slightly lower ageing potential
slides.8.question: What is the Dão's most important flagship white grape, often called "Portugal's Chardonnay"?
slides.8.explanation: Encruzado is the flagship white grape of the Dão DOC. On granite soils and in a cool climate it shows crisp minerality, and after oak ageing it develops cream and flint complexity. With strong ageing potential, it is hailed as "Portugal's Chardonnay".
slides.9.question: In which Portuguese region does Touriga Nacional originate?
slides.9.explanation: Touriga Nacional originated in the Dão and was later planted more widely in the Douro, Alentejo and elsewhere. In the Dão's granite highlands and cool climate it shows its most delicate and elegant side, in sharp contrast to the full, robust style of the Douro.
